speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. How old is the child, and when did you first notice the bleeding episodes and skin spots?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the child experienced any recent viral illnesses, and have you noticed any bleeding from the gastrointestinal tract or in the urine? Please also let me know if there is any family history of bleeding disorders or if the child has been taking any new medications recently.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the child experienced any joint pain or bleeding into the muscles, and is there any family history of bleeding disorders? I also need to know if the child has had a recent viral illness or fever.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text: To help narrow down the cause, I need to know if the child has had a recent viral illness or fever, and if there is any family history of bleeding disorders. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the platelet count is normal, I need to evaluate the coagulation cascade next. REQUEST TEST: PT, PTT, Bleeding_Time

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal platelet count and coagulation studies, I suspect a platelet function defect like Glanzmann thrombasthenia or Bernard-Soulier syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Platelet_function_assay

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ELISA Binding Assay: Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text: The deficient GIIb/IIIa receptors confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
